Visit note | 2025-09-02 03:00 PM | Dr. Sabrina Chowdhury, Cardiology | Patient: Mehedi Shikder, 53, male. Mr. Shikder attends for review and reports concerns relating to a father who had a heart attack at 55 and high cholesterol on a routine test. He works as a tailor, and this finding was picked up on a pre-employment test in Badda. He maintains his usual daily routine but is anxious about his cardiovascular health. He has Type 2 diabetes mellitus. He denies chest pain, palpitations, or shortness of breath. On examination: LDL cholesterol 5.6 mmol/L, BP 136/84 mmHg, pulse 91 bpm, weight 88 kg. Heart sounds are normal. Assessment: Dyslipidaemia. Plan: chronic follow-up: continue current medicines, no new prescription issued. He was advised to reduce fried food, red meat, and ghee, walk 30 minutes daily, and aim to lose 3 kg. Follow-up in 3 months with a repeat lipid profile.
